site.name: Hannahuel
site.intro: I'm 22, and this December I will hold a master's degree in land and property development from Texas A&M. I move fast, I learn faster, and I'm ready to turn raw land into feasible, well-documented deals, with a writer's eye for every detail.
about: I am 22, and in December 2026 I will finish my **Master of Land & Property Development** at Texas A&M. I didn't take the long way around: I finished my bachelor's in December 2024 and started graduate school the very next semester, because I already knew what I wanted to build.

I came to real estate through words. I earned a **B.A. in English** at the University of Houston, where I also tutored and graded for ESL students through Phi Beta Delta and earned my TEAL certification. That background taught me to read closely, research carefully, and explain complicated things plainly, which turns out to be most of what a land deal asks of you.

Today I am completing a **Master of Land & Property Development** at Texas A&M. In LDEV 651 I reviewed and revised easements, entitlements, and deeds, and evaluated ventures through capital structure and feasibility. For my capstone I am structuring a **1,500-acre mixed-use development** in Laredo for a client, pulling live market data into an analysis of what drives the project's value.

This summer I interned with **Buzzy Development/Penz Homes** in Dallas, working on deal structuring, budgets, marketing, and researching modular and prefabricated construction. Before that, more than a year as a Fleet Agent at American Airlines taught me how to stay precise when timelines are tight and the rules are strict.

Next, I am looking for roles in **land and master-planned community development**, as a **development associate**, or with the public agencies and consultants who shape how places grow. I am based in Houston, value hybrid flexibility, and am glad to travel for the work. I bring the energy of someone at the start of her career and the discipline of someone who has already been working hard to get here: I am eager to learn from experienced developers, quick to take on responsibility, and ready to contribute from day one.
Off the clock you will find me training for my next running event, assembling a puzzle, or satisfying my sweet tooth with a new dessert recipe.

pins.title: My development philosophy
pins.meta: What I believe good development looks like

cover.text: Read the site, the market, and the paperwork closely. End with a place people are glad was built.

overview: Good development starts with reading the site, the market, and the paperwork closely, and ends with a place people are glad was built.

I came to real estate from English, so I trust close reading. A deed, an easement, or a utility district agreement can quietly decide whether a project works, and I would rather find that out in due diligence than at closing. I try to bring the same care to the model: name the assumptions, test them against real data, and change course when the facts change.

I believe the best projects create durable value for the community around them, not only for the people who fund them. Large sites like the 1,500 acres in my capstone shape how people live for decades, so the mix of uses, open space, and infrastructure matter as much as the return.
Most of all, I believe in clear communication. A deal that the team, the lender, and the community understand the same way is a deal that holds together.
